data.typical_vehicles: Haul trucks, graders, excavators, LDVs, surface and underground support vehicles
data.service_need: High-intensity A/C and auto electrical maintenance; units operate in extreme heat and dust, accelerating compressor wear, refrigerant loss, and electrical faults. Onsite service capability is essential due to equipment size and remote mine locations.
data.service_frequency: High â€“ monthly or per-shift inspections for critical equipment; major overhauls at scheduled shutdowns (quarterly or biannual)
data.procurement_method: Formal tender or negotiated contract â€“ most large mines (AngloGold, Sibanye, Amplats, Kumba) require approved vendor registration and SLA-based agreements. Outsourced service preferred when mines lack specialist in-house capability.
data.decision_makers: Fleet managers, mine maintenance superintendents, procurement officers
data.value_level: Very High â€“ long-duration SLA contracts with guaranteed callout volumes; equipment downtime costs are extremely high

data.typical_vehicles: Long-haul trucks (Class 7â€“8), refrigerated vehicles, light commercial vehicles
data.service_need: Truck cab A/C maintenance and repair; auto electrical diagnostics (alternators, starters, wiring); compliance with roadworthy and COR requirements
data.service_frequency: Scheduled every 6 months or at mileage intervals; breakdown callouts as needed
data.procurement_method: Mix of in-house workshop supplemented by outsourced specialists; larger operators (e.g., Barloworld Logistics, Unitrans) use preferred-supplier panels. Smaller operators make ad-hoc decisions.
data.decision_makers: Fleet managers, workshop managers, transport owners
data.value_level: High â€“ large fleet volumes; mobile or depot-based service preferred to reduce vehicle downtime

data.typical_vehicles: Sedans, SUVs, LDVs, buses, emergency vehicles for national departments, municipalities, SOEs
data.service_need: Routine A/C servicing, regas, and fault repair; auto electrical diagnostics aligned to manufacturer specifications
data.service_frequency: Annual or scheduled per km/hour intervals; governed by gFleet policy (Scheduled and Unscheduled Maintenance categories)
data.procurement_method: Formal public tender (eTender portal); CIDB registration and BEE compliance required. National government managed through Government Motor Transport (gFleet). SOEs such as Transnet, Eskom, PRASA, and municipalities procure separately.
data.decision_makers: Fleet management units within departments; supply chain management officials; gFleet programme managers
data.value_level: Medium-High â€“ large vehicle volumes but price-sensitive and compliance-heavy; slow procurement cycles

data.typical_vehicles: Bulldozers, TLBs, cranes, articulated dump trucks, site LDVs
data.service_need: A/C compressor repairs, refrigerant top-ups, electrical fault diagnosis in high-vibration, dusty environments; battery and alternator servicing
data.service_frequency: Linked to project cycles and seasonal shutdown schedules; peak maintenance before and after summer construction seasons
data.procurement_method: Mix of direct contractor relationship and equipment rental company arrangements; smaller construction firms outsource; larger contractors (WBHO, Murray & Roberts, Aveng) use in-house or approved-supplier models
data.decision_makers: Site managers, plant and equipment managers, procurement officers
data.value_level: Medium-High â€“ site-based service contracts with repeat access; equipment downtime directly impacts project delivery
